title: Temperature-Dependent Operando Liquid Cell S/TEM: Modulating Electrochemical Kinetics and Beam-Induced Effects
content: The advancement of sample holder technology for scanning/transmission electron microscopy (S/TEM) has enabled groundbreaking research across multiple disciplines. However, limitations still exist. Traditional cryo-holders allow imaging of beam-sensitive low-Z materials, such as biological samples, in vitreous ice, but they primarily maintain a frozen sample at low temperatures without permitting fluid exchange or electrical biasing. Some commercially available cryo-holders incorporate MEMS-based sample supports that enable electrical biasing at low temperatures, but these supports cannot withstand the typical plunge-freezing process. As a result, samples must be imaged in a “dry” state, and the open-cell nature of these holders prevents fluid exchange.
